description: Render a short branded video (9:16 vertical by default; also square and landscape) and save it to the media library as an mp4 — returning a media id create_post takes as mediaIds. Either a storyboard (template storyboard: the scenes given in `scenes`, in order, with an optional music bed) or one of the fixed, silent templates in list_video_templates. Pick the canvas by where it goes: vertical for Reels, TikTok, Shorts and Stories (every word is kept clear of the buttons and captions those apps draw over a video, and inside the feed's 4:5 crop), square for X, LinkedIn and other feeds, landscape only for YouTube or a website. Fewer, shorter lines read better: three features beat five. It lays out the user's own pictures, clips and words — no generative model draws anything. It costs 25 of the workspace's monthly credits, taken before rendering and handed back if the render fails; once the month's credits are spent it is refused with the balance — tell the user, do not retry. Render only what the user asked for: confirm the template, the headline and the pictures first when they have not said. Pictures come from the media library: upload_media for a file, capture_screenshot for the website, import_app_screenshots for the App Store or Google Play listing. A shot given by mediaId must be an image. The brand name, tagline and icon are filled in from the brand profile and the workspace unless overridden here; set accent to a #rrggbb colour to give the video the brand's colour. Rendering takes one to five minutes on a shared box, a 30-second storyboard the most. The call waits up to `wait` seconds (default 40) reporting progress, then returns the finished video — or the render's id and status when it needs longer, in which case call get_video with the id. The result names any field the template leaves out. Nothing is posted anywhere: the video sits in the private library until a post carrying it is published.
